text:
Elaine A.: Hey team — NeonBridge (enterprise health analytics) wants to run a POC next week. They plan to bring a custom ‘llama70b-neo-v2’ variant (FP16 -> 4-bit quant planned). Questions: 1) Can we host this in Dedicated or Private? 2) KV cache compatibility and memory footprint for their 4k context workloads? 3) Pricing guidance for reserved burst capacity + KMS integration. Need a quick triage so AE can scope the SOW.
Samir (SE): +1. Quick notes: we’ve seen similar 70b variants quantize ok with our q4_0 path but need a compatibility scan for rmsnorm/rope variants. We should run the variant through the catalog ingestion script and a quick perf sweep.
Mike I.: Dedicated and Private both OK. Private if they need HSM-backed KMS and VPC peering. Dedicated can do KMS via customer-managed keys across our partner KMS, but HSM-only requirements push them to Private.
NeonBridge POC: They need SOC2 + data isolation. HSM is preferred for keys. Also want to confirm tokenization — they fine-tuned with a custom tokenizer.
Sofia S. (Security): SOC2 is fine. For HSM we need a Private deployment note in the contract. Also: ask them to fill the security questionnaire section on key handling and retention. We’ll need sample model weights checksum before onboarding.
Samir (SE): For tokenizer + custom embeddings: recommend they provide the tokenizer files and a minimal model package. We’ll run an ingest test. If tokenizer differs, we may need an adapter layer; that usually adds ~5–10% latency.
Elaine A.: Timeline: customer wants demo in 10 days. Sales needs pricing estimate today. Can we ballpark reserved capacity + burst for 100 qps with 4k seq?
Mike I.: Ballpark: reserved baseline for a single 70b quant variant ~ $18k/month (depends on region/hardware), burst add-on ~ $6k/month. Private infra + HSM adds platform license (one-time) ~ $50k–80k + infra run rate. I'll confirm after a quick capacity calc.
Samir (SE): Also note: KV cache mem for 4k windows w/ this model and 4-bit quant ~ 18–24GB per concurrent stream in worst-case. With batching we can reduce concurrency needs. Suggest default cache TTL 30s for POC.
NeonBridge POC: That KV number is higher than expected. Can we do prefix caching or chunking to reduce mem?
Samir (SE): Yes. Two options: 1) prefix KV caching to reuse short prompts 2) split long contexts and stream with partial cache. We can provide a sample config. Example snippet:
```
model_variant: llama70b-neo-v2-q4_0
enable_kv_cache: true
kv_ttl_sec: 30
batch_config:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_wait_ms: 15
```
Elaine A.: Good. Sofia — can you own the questionnaire ask and list required artifacts for onboarding? I’ll send the pricing and draft SOW to NeonBridge after we confirm.
Sofia S. (Security): I’ll send a checklist: 1) SOC attestation 2) KMS/HSM requirement doc 3) model weights checksum + provenance 4) data retention policy 5) network architecture for Private/VPC peering. Expect my note in ~2 hours.
Mike I.: I’ll run a quick capacity calc and a 1-hour perf sweep on a staging 70b quant image tonight. Will report numbers (p99 latency, tokens/sec) by EOD.
Samir (SE): I’ll queue the variant through the ingestion pipeline once they share the package. Also will run a short eval using their prompt set to check regression against baseline.
Elaine A.: Perfect — action items: @NeonBridge POC share model package + tokenizer + SFDC opp id; @Sofia S. send checklist; @Mike I. perf numbers tonight; @Samir run ingest/eval. I’ll update the customer and aim for a demo slot next Wednesday. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deploy job queued for perf-sweep-staging-70b-quant (#4728) — ETA 45m.
NeonBridge POC: Sending package via s3 link and the SFDC opp in DM. Thanks everyone.
